text:
Recent work supports adaptive mixtures of persistent preferences and transient interests, but does not establish a universally optimal recent window. [TLSTSRec (2024/2025)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) combines temporal information with personalized adaptive fusion of long/short-term sequences. [E-NSDE (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) explicitly models irregular interaction intervals and connects longer gaps with predictive uncertainty. These motivate conditioning preference fusion on elapsed time rather than sequence position alone.

State-space models offer linear sequence scaling, although short histories remain a concern: [MaTrRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19239) identifies weaknesses of standalone Mamba on short sequences and combines it with Transformer attention. [SIGMA (AAAI 2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33336) adds input-dependent gating and a GRU for short-term dependencies. [MaTra4LS (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0020025526003762) separates long-term Mamba representations from a dynamic-window Transformer. [HM2Rec (AAAI 2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38567) uses token-dependent expert routing, though its hyperbolic graph/VGAE machinery makes it a less lightweight starting point.

Practical hypothesis for this benchmark: retain SASRec and add a small gate over last-item, several recency-weighted pools, and whole-history pooling, using observed history length and timestamp-gap statistics. This is an inferred experiment, not a demonstrated result from these papers. Compare against each component alone, fixed-window variants, and a gate without timestamps; inspect validation HR@10 by history length and gap size. Deletion sensitivity establishes dependence on removed events, not the best recency scale or identifiable latent intent switching. Published gains under other protocols do not establish gains under the pinned evaluator.
